questions.q: The editorial quotes a passage from the magazine’s first issue about the rose bush. What does it say?
options: Life, like the rose bush, holds both flowers and thorns; this is how God made the world, and we must fit in with it
Yes. We cannot have things any other way.
Flowers fade, so they are not worth tending
Not quite. The article says: Life, like the rose bush, holds both flowers and thorns; this is how God made the world, and we must fit in with it.
Roses grow only in certain soils
Not quite. The article says: Life, like the rose bush, holds both flowers and thorns; this is how God made the world, and we must fit in with it.
Thorns should be removed before flowers are enjoyed
Not quite. The article says: Life, like the rose bush, holds both flowers and thorns; this is how God made the world, and we must fit in with it.
questions.rationale: “Just as the rose bush, along with its exquisite flowers, also possesses piercing thorns, so also does life contain an amalgam of both pleasing and displeasing objects.”

questions.q: Hiding in the cave with pursuers at its mouth, what did the Prophet say to reassure Abu Bakr?
options: “We shall leave by another way”
Not quite. The article says: “How can you be apprehensive about the two with whom is a third, the third being God Himself?”.
“Help is coming from Madinah”
Not quite. The article says: “How can you be apprehensive about the two with whom is a third, the third being God Himself?”.
“They will not look inside”
Not quite. The article says: “How can you be apprehensive about the two with whom is a third, the third being God Himself?”.
“How can you be apprehensive about the two with whom is a third, the third being God Himself?”
Right. Complete trust in God’s help.
questions.rationale: “The Prophet reassured him, ‘How can you be apprehensive about the two with whom is a third, the third being God Himself?’”

options: The matter should be decided later
Not quite. The article says: God sent the Prophet as a guide to humanity, not as a collector of taxes.
God sent the Prophet as a guide to humanity, not as a collector of taxes
Well read. The mission came before the treasury.
Revenue must be protected at all costs
Not quite. The article says: God sent the Prophet as a guide to humanity, not as a collector of taxes.
The governor should raise other taxes
Not quite. The article says: God sent the Prophet as a guide to humanity, not as a collector of taxes.
questions.rationale: “Umar bin Abdul Aziz replied: God Almighty sent the Prophet Muhammad as a guide to humanity, not as a collector of taxes.”

questions.q: To what does the article compare someone who takes up leadership without the necessary knowledge and understanding?
options: A person who jumps into a river without knowing how to swim
Yes. And he bears the blame for where he leads others.
A merchant without capital
Not quite. The article says: A person who jumps into a river without knowing how to swim.
A traveller without a map
Not quite. The article says: A person who jumps into a river without knowing how to swim.
A farmer who sows in winter
Not quite. The article says: A person who jumps into a river without knowing how to swim.
questions.rationale: “To swim in the river, only that person will venture who knows the art of swimming. Similarly, only a person who has fulfilled essential conditions of leadership should come into the field of leadership.”

questions.q: On becoming Caliph, what did Abu Bakr tell the people about the weak and the strong among them?
options: The strong would be given charge of the weak
Not quite. The article says: The weak would be strong in his eyes until given their due, and the strong weak until they gave what they owed.
The weak would be sent away from the city
Not quite. The article says: The weak would be strong in his eyes until given their due, and the strong weak until they gave what they owed.
All would be treated according to rank
Not quite. The article says: The weak would be strong in his eyes until given their due, and the strong weak until they gave what they owed.
The weak would be strong in his eyes until given their due, and the strong weak until they gave what they owed
Correct. “I am no better than you… when you see me waver, set me straight.”
questions.rationale: “The weak among you will be the strongest until I have ensured that they received what is rightfully theirs. The strong among you I will look upon as the weakest, until I have made sure that they pay their due.”

questions.q: Which three actions did the Prophet call the most difficult?
options: Fasting, travelling and keeping awake
Not quite. The article says: Being fair to others where one’s own interest is involved, giving from one’s own possessions, and remembering God at all times.
Being fair to others where one’s own interest is involved, giving from one’s own possessions, and remembering God at all times
Right. Each asks one to go against the self.
Trading, building and farming
Not quite. The article says: Being fair to others where one’s own interest is involved, giving from one’s own possessions, and remembering God at all times.
Learning, teaching and writing
Not quite. The article says: Being fair to others where one’s own interest is involved, giving from one’s own possessions, and remembering God at all times.
questions.rationale: “Being fair with others on matters concerning oneself; helping others by giving from one’s own possessions; and remembering God at all times.”

questions.q: How does the article describe patience?
options: Not passivity, but wise, well-planned action that takes the facts and consequences into account
Well reasoned. Impatience is leaping without thought.
Waiting and doing nothing
Not quite. The article says: Not passivity, but wise, well-planned action that takes the facts and consequences into account.
Hiding one’s feelings
Not quite. The article says: Not passivity, but wise, well-planned action that takes the facts and consequences into account.
Accepting defeat quietly
Not quite. The article says: Not passivity, but wise, well-planned action that takes the facts and consequences into account.
questions.rationale: “Patience is neither a passive attitude nor any kind of inaction… Patience means wisdom-based thinking. It means planning your strategy, assessing your resources.”

questions.q: According to the sayings of the Prophet collected in the article, for what may one pray to God?
options: For every need, however small – even something like a shoelace
Yes. “Praying is the essence of worship.”
Only in times of danger
Not quite. The article says: For every need, however small – even something like a shoelace.
Only for the next world
Not quite. The article says: For every need, however small – even something like a shoelace.
Only for great matters
Not quite. The article says: For every need, however small – even something like a shoelace.
questions.rationale: “Praying is a means of asking God for the fulfillment of all our needs no matter how mundane or insignificant as even a shoe lace.”

questions.q: The reviewer of “The Final Journey” quotes a striking line from the book about death. What is it?
options: “Death is the end of every story”
Not quite. The article says: “Death is the greatest teacher, but man lives out his life as if there was no such thing awaiting him”.
“Death is the greatest teacher, but man lives out his life as if there was no such thing awaiting him”
Exactly. It set the reviewer asking how prepared she was.
“Death comes only to the old”
Not quite. The article says: “Death is the greatest teacher, but man lives out his life as if there was no such thing awaiting him”.
“Death is a sleep from which none wake”
Not quite. The article says: “Death is the greatest teacher, but man lives out his life as if there was no such thing awaiting him”.
questions.rationale: “Death is the greatest teacher, but man lives out his life as if there was no such thing awaiting him at the end of life’s journey.”

questions.q: Abraham settled his family in a barren valley and prayed that they be given fruits. What wisdom does the commentary see in this?
options: Fruit is the healthiest food
Not quite. The article says: Provision arriving where none could be grown would awaken an extraordinary sense of gratitude.
Trade would make them wealthy
Not quite. The article says: Provision arriving where none could be grown would awaken an extraordinary sense of gratitude.
Provision arriving where none could be grown would awaken an extraordinary sense of gratitude
Well read. “So that they may be grateful.”
The valley would soon become fertile
Not quite. The article says: Provision arriving where none could be grown would awaken an extraordinary sense of gratitude.
questions.rationale: “With the provision of extraordinary bounties, extraordinary feelings of gratefulness arise in man. This was the wisdom which was hidden in Abraham’s prayer.”
